critique_of_gto_peer: GTO peer arrives at the same FOLD verdict with a similar 90/10 mix; reasoning is solid on the realization-haircut math and correctly identifies that AJo lacks a backdoor flush component that other A-high continues have. Minor over-statement: peer credits ~22-25% raw equity and treats the call as merely thin, but the OOP-EARLY structural problem (two villains BEHIND, not closing as I mis-stated R1) is under-weighted in the framing. The 0.85 realization factor peer cites is too generous for OOP-EARLY-3-way; 0.70-0.75 is closer to truth. Net: same verdict, math slightly soft.
critique_of_range_construction_peer: Range-construction peer reaches FOLD at only MEDIUM confidence with a 25% CALL mix, which is too generous. Peer is correct that BB's continuing range at this node is populated by stronger A-highs with backdoor flush components and that AJo is the marginal cut; peer is also correct that two flats behind the c-bet compress UTG's bluff frequency. However, peer's 25% CALL frequency overweights the A-blocker unblocking UTG's bluffs — in MW with two cold-callers behind, the squeeze-from-behind threat alone disqualifies most of the CALL frequency that single-villain analysis would preserve.
critique_of_sonnet_majority: Three CALL voters (1, 2, 3) argue: (a) ~18% pot odds + 6 overcard outs + backdoor diamond on Ad + nut-A blocker = thin peel; (b) BB's defending range is widest at table. This does NOT survive MW scrutiny: voter 1 admits 55/45 LOW confidence and acknowledges the realization swing; voter 2 invents a backdoor nut FD that doesn't exist (Ad alone with rainbow board = runner-runner only, near-zero EV); voter 3 hallucinates a gutshot then walks it back mid-reasoning. All three under-weight the OOP-EARLY structure with TWO villains behind who can raise and the cold-caller-cap implying value-heavy continuance. Voters 4 and 5 (FOLD) correctly identify the structural deficit and the value-heavy multiway c-bet signal.
critique_of_opus_tierup: Opus FOLD reasoning is high-quality from the MW lens: explicitly names OOP-EARLY squeeze-pressure asymmetry, correctly flags HJ + CO raise-threat on the c-bet, and identifies reverse-implied-odds on dirty turn cards (A-turn gives villain Ax pairs, J-turn gives QJ/KJ/JT two-pair). Opus's pot-odds analysis (18% face value vs ~28-30% realisation-adjusted requirement) is the cleanest MW framing in the room. The MEDIUM confidence rating is slightly soft given how decisively the structural factors stack against CALL; I would rate this HIGH. Otherwise Opus is correctly grounded.
revised_reasoning: Round 1 verdict FOLD HIGH stands, with one MW-framing correction acknowledged: hero is OOP-EARLY (not closing action — HJ and CO still behind on this street's action chain), which STRENGTHENS the FOLD case I made in R1 rather than weakening it. The peer + Opus convergence on FOLD plus the 2-of-5 Sonnet FOLD voters (the two with the strongest structural reasoning) confirms the multiway specialist call. Mix frequency revised slightly to 85/15 (from pure FOLD) to acknowledge the range-construction peer's valid point that the A-blocker + closing-grid balance argument supports a small mixing frequency — but I reject the 25% CALL frequency as too generous for OOP-EARLY-MW. The decisive MW-specialist drivers: (1) OOP-EARLY with TWO villains BEHIND means any CALL invites a raise from HJ/CO's range-capped-but-value-heavy continuance (sets, Tx-suited, overpairs, OESDs); the cold-caller-cap doesn't help when the continuing-after-cap composition is denser in made hands than air. (2) Multiway c-bet into 3 villains on T-high dry board is a high-conviction value signal — UTG's range here is ~55-60% pair-or-better, against which AJo has 6 overcard outs but 3-5 of them are DIRTY (AT, KJ, QJ, JT dominate hero on hits). (3) Realization factor 0.70-0.75 OOP-EARLY-MW collapses raw 22-25% equity to ~16-18% effective, exactly at face-value pot odds with zero margin before accounting for the squeeze-threat tax and reverse-implied-odds tax. (4) BB's defending range at this node is populated by hands with backdoor flush components (suited A-highs), pairs with SDV (small/mid PPs), and connected draws (87s, 75s, 65s) — AJo with no backdoor flush, no straight component, and dirty overcards is the canonical marginal-fold to construct without over-defending. RAISE remains dominated (no fold equity vs 3 declared-continuing villains, hand blocks zero value and unblocks bluffs). CALL is the losing temptation; FOLD is the multiway-specialist call. Confidence HIGH.
